summary.one_liner: OpenAgents is an open platform for hosting and using language agents (Data, Plugins, and Web agents) through a chat-based web UI, with the full source code released for localhost or Docker deployment.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes three agents with a chat web UI: a Data Agent for data analysis with Python/SQL and data tools (search, handle, manipulate, visualize), a Plugins Agent that integrates over 200 third-party plugins with support for combined use and automatic plugin selection, and a Web Agent that uses a Chrome extension to browse websites autonomously (examples include Google Maps navigation, posting to Twitter, and filling Google Forms). The repository contains a Flask backend, a Next.js frontend with the WeBot Chrome extension, and a real_agents/ folder where each agent lives in its own directory with shared adapters. The README also includes a tutorial on extending the platform with new agents, LLMs (registered in backend/api/language_model.py), and plugins. A docker-compose setup is provided, along with notes on GPU use and Auto Plugin model downloads from Hugging Face.
use_cases: Analyze datasets with Python or SQL through a chat interface
Call third-party tools like weather or shopping plugins from chat
Automate browser tasks such as Google Maps routing or filling web forms
Self-host a multi-agent chat platform on localhost or with Docker
Build and register a new language agent or plugin on top of the platform
Run real-world language agent evaluations and research experiments
how_to_run: Localhost: follow the backend and frontend README files in the backend/ and frontend/ folders
Docker: set KAGGLE_USER and KAGGLE_KEY in the Dockerfile if using Kaggle datasets
Docker: set NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_ENDPOINT in frontend/Dockerfile if not running locally
Run `docker compose build` in the project root, setting OPENAI_API_KEY (or OPENAI_API_BASE) in docker-compose.yml
Run `docker compose up -d` to start all services
notable: Three hosted agents (Data, Plugins, Web) with a free public demo
Plugins Agent supports 200+ plugins, combined use, and auto plugin selection
Web Agent is driven by a bundled Chrome extension (webot_extension.zip)
Lemur open-source foundation models for language agents are mentioned as matching ChatGPT on 15 agent tasks
Structured as 'one agent, one folder' under real_agents/ to make extension easier
caveats: The README says the Docker deployment is under development and may be slower or have non-working functions; the source code is recommended for a more robust setup
Auto Plugin downloads weight files from Hugging Face, which may time out in some regions
Pulling code from before 10/26/2023 loses local chat history because key names changed
